examples.explain: Both -1, 0, 1 and 5, 6, 7 have length 3. The duplicate 1 doesn't extend anything.

hints: Sorting makes it easy but costs O(n log n). What does sorting really help you check?
With a set you can ask "is x + 1 present?" in O(1). From which numbers should you start counting?
Only start a count at x when x − 1 is NOT in the set. Then each number is visited a constant number of times.

insight.oneLiner: Put everything in a set; a number starts a run iff num − 1 is missing - only walk forward from those.

recall.a: Skip num unless num − 1 is absent.
recall.q: What single check keeps the set solution O(n)?

recall.a: Deduplicate (or skip equal neighbours) - they neither extend nor break a run.
recall.q: How should duplicates be handled when sorting?

signals: O(n) required where sorting is the obvious approach
insight.why: Without the start check, a run of length L is re-walked from each of its L numbers - O(n²) on a long run. With it, each number is stepped over at most once in total.

oneLiner: Put everything in a set; a number starts a run iff num − 1 is missing - only walk forward from those.

pitfalls.explain: When sorted, equal neighbours should be skipped - resetting the run on them undercounts.
pitfalls.title: Duplicates broke a run

pitfalls.explain: 1, 1, 2 is a run of length 2, not 3.
pitfalls.title: Counted duplicates as part of a run

pitfalls.explain: An empty array has longest run 0.
pitfalls.title: Mishandled the empty array

solutions.idea: After deduplicating and sorting, consecutive runs are contiguous - count them in one scan.
solutions.name: Sort and scan

footnotes.text: Only extending from run starts is the whole trick: every number is walked over at most once across all runs, so the total work is O(n).

solutions.idea: Only start counting from numbers with no predecessor; walk forward with O(1) lookups.
solutions.name: Hash set from run starts

starter:
class Solution:
    def longestConsecutive(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
statement:
Given an unsorted integer array `nums`, return the length of the **longest run of consecutive integers** (like `4, 5, 6, 7`) whose values all appear in `nums`. The values can be anywhere in the array.

Aim for O(n) time.
title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
